newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks slump in thin trade, banks in focus.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks slump in thin trade, banks in focus.

text.p: Madrid shares closed sharply lower on Tuesday, with thin volume and weakness on Wall Street exaggerating the slide in prices as traders took profits.
Banks were at the centre of trade after some disappointing first half results. Popular lost 5.29 percent to 35,990 pesetas and Bankinter shed 2.67 percent to 26,600 pesetas.
Telefonica shed 2.1 percent to 4,430 pesetas, impacted by a profit warning from U.S. partner MCI last week, analysts said. Shares are seen supported at 4,400 pesetas.
The general index fell 8.31 points, 1.32 percent, to 619.79 and the Ibex shed 105.30 points, 1.47 percent, to 7,064.12.
Dealers said the bourse has been need of consolidation for some time. Bank results which undershot forecasts had helped to take some of the steam out of the market, they added.
But thin trade, as many foreign investors start holidays, was notable. A dealer at a Spanish bank predicted see-sawing indices for the short-term.
"We'll move sideways, and trade will stay thin. But this will serve as consolidation, and really we're in need of a breather before pushing up again after the summer," he said.
